Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG Legal Opinion No. 75 s. 2011 NOV 10 2011 MR. SOTERO D. ALARCON Busuanga, Palawan Dear Mr. Alarcon: This pertains to your letter regarding the SK Federation Presiden of Busuanga, Palawan. Per your letter, the S.K. Federation President of Busua4ga, Palawan served for two consecutive terms. He was elected during the synchronibed Barangay and S.K. elections in October 29, 2007 and was re-elected during the SK election last October 25, 2010. At present, he is still the SK Federation President ånd sit as ex-officio member of the Sangguniang Bayan for two consecutive terms. Hence, you are now seeking our legal opinion on the following queries: Ill) Is his position to serve twice, legal? What are the basis aside from Section 428 and 429 of Republic Act No. 7160 (sic)? 2) If illegal, what are also the basis? And what will happen to him? Can he be removed from Office? Who will remove him? Can role of succession be applied (sic) ? At the outset, may we invite your attention to Sections 2 and 6 of Republic ct No. 9164 otherwise known as "An Act providing for Synchronized Barangay nd Sangguniang Kabataan Elections, Amending Republic Act No. 7160, as amended, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991 and for other which provide and we quote. "Section 2. Term of office. The term of office of all barangay and sangguniang kabataan officials after the effectivity of this Act shall be three (3) years. " No barangay_ elective official shall serve for more than three (3) consecutive terms in the same position: Provided, however, that the term of office shall be reckoned from the 1994 barangay elections. Voluntary renunciation of office for any length of time shall not be considered as interruption in the continuity of service for the full term for which the elective official was elected. Section 6. Section 424 of Republic Act No. 7160, othexwise known as Local Government Code of 1991, is hereby amended to read as follows:

I -2- "Section 424. Katipunan ng Kabataan. The katipunan ng Kabataan shall be composed of Filipino citizens actually residing in the barangay for at least six (6) months, who are fifteen (15) but less than eighteen 18 years of age on the day of the election, and who are duly registered in the list of the sangguniang kabataan or in the official barangay list in the custody of barangay secretary. " The aforequoted provisions particularly Section 6 of R.A 9164 clearly pro ides for the age qualification in the Sangguniang Kabataan elections which is fifteek (15) years old but less than eighteen years old during the SK election. Applying the above-cited provisions to your query, since your Sanggu iang Kabataan Federation President was still below eighteen years old during the time that he was reelected therefore his election as Sangguniang Kabataan Chairman is valid. Please note further that the term of office of the Sanggunian Kabataan Chairman and members under Section 2 of RA 9164 shall not be more than three consecutive terms. While Section 2 of RA 9164 provides for the term of Barangay elective officials, SK officials are considered barangay elective officials. Such conclusion is supported by the Decision of the Supreme Court in the case of Francis King L. Marquez vs. Comelec [G.R. No. 127318, August 25, 1999] where it was uled that "An SK Chairman is considered a barangay official under Section 387 (a) of the Omnibus Election Code which provides that "there shall be in each barangay a punong barangay, seven (7) barangay members, the sangguniang kabataan chairman, a barangay secretary and a barangay treasurer." Such being the case, the three (3) consecutive term limit is also applicable to the Sangguniang Kabataan Chairman, provided however, the age qualification bf the Sangguniang Kabataan must be observed. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, Any. JES S B.D UE Director 111 LS:94/11
